# Diagnostics baseline: gtfparser vs real tf

Generated by `scripts/warn_baseline.py` from `scripts/warncheck.py --json` (engine commit `cac3adb`). 
Regenerate: `go build -o /tmp/warn_gtfrun ./cmd/gtfrun && . scripts/env.sh && python3 scripts/warncheck.py --json /tmp/w.json --no-gate && python3 scripts/warn_baseline.py /tmp/w.json > testdata/warnings/BASELINE.md`.

## Summary

- catalog: **439** entries, **257** testable, 182 untestable
- cases run: **257**
- status: `OK` 235, `body` 9, `missing` 8, `body+missing` 5
- mismatch classes (a case can have several): body 14, context 0, missing in gtfparser 13, extra in gtfparser 0
- body-only comparison (`--ignore-context`): **235 of 257** cases already match exactly
- real tf crashed in: none. (Earlier probing found that real tf of this build crashes with signal 11 after printing `division by zero` inside a macro; that case is `expr.813` run at file level, so it is unaffected.)

(priority 1 = most likely hit by a real script or user.)

## Context prefix format

Real tf prefixes errors with `% [<file>, line N: ][<command>[ -<opt>]: ]` (`eprefix()` in tfio.c). 
`<file>` is the file being `/load`ed, `lines N-M` for a backslash-continued command; `<command>` is the *innermost* 
running thing: the builtin's upper-case name (`DEF`, `EVAL`, `UNDEF`; `/test` and bare expressions show none), a macro's name, 
a function's name (`mod: `), or `#N` for an unnamed macro. Typed at the prompt there is no file part. Warnings add `Warning: ` after it. 
gtfparser builds the same prefix (`Interp.warn`); the table shows the probe cases of the context rules.

| case | real tf | gtfparser |
|---|---|---|
| ctx.file-line | `<FILE>, line 3: nofunc: no such function` | `<FILE>, line 3: nofunc: no such function` |
| ctx.macro | `<FILE>, line 2: f: nofunc: no such function` | `<FILE>, line 2: f: nofunc: no such function` |
| ctx.macro-nested | `<FILE>, line 3: inner: nofunc: no such function` | `<FILE>, line 3: inner: nofunc: no such function` |
| ctx.multiline | `<FILE>, lines 2-3: nofunc: no such function` | `<FILE>, lines 2-3: nofunc: no such function` |
| ctx.eval | `<FILE>, line 1: nofunc: no such function` | `<FILE>, line 1: nofunc: no such function` |
| ctx.trigger | `<FILE>, line 2: trg: nofunc: no such function` | `<FILE>, line 2: trg: nofunc: no such function` |
| ctx.hook | `<FILE>, line 2: zzz: no such command or macro \| <FILE>, line 2: #751: nofunc: no such function` | `<FILE>, line 2: zzz: no such command or macro \| <FILE>, line 2: #751: nofunc: no such function` |
| ctx.load-nested | `Loading commands from <DIR>/sub/inner.tf. \| <DIR>/sub/inner.tf, line 2: nofunc: no such function` | `Loading commands from <DIR>/sub/inner.tf. \| <DIR>/sub/inner.tf, line 2: nofunc: no such function` |
| ctx.option-suffix | `<FILE>, line 1: DEF -Z: invalid option \| <FILE>, line 1: DEF: options: -p<integer> -c<integer> -b<string> ...` | `<FILE>, line 1: DEF -Z: invalid option \| <FILE>, line 1: DEF: options: -p<integer> -c<integer> -b<string> ...` |
| ctx.function-name | `<FILE>, line 1: mod: real value too large to convert to integer` | `<FILE>, line 1: mod: real value too large to convert to integer` |
| ctx.builtin-in-macro | `<FILE>, line 2: UNDEF: Macro "nope" was not defined.` | `<FILE>, line 2: UNDEF: Macro "nope" was not defined.` |
| ctx.nonexistent-command | `<FILE>, line 1: nosuchcommand: no such command or macro` | `<FILE>, line 1: nosuchcommand: no such command or macro` |
| ctx.nonexistent-in-macro | `<FILE>, line 2: h: nosuchcommand: no such command or macro` | `<FILE>, line 2: h: nosuchcommand: no such command or macro` |
| ctx.typed | `nofunc: no such function` | `nofunc: no such function` |
| ctx.typed-macro | `f: nofunc: no such function` | `f: nofunc: no such function` |
| ctx.typed-builtin | `UNDEF: Macro "nosuchmacro" was not defined.` | `UNDEF: Macro "nosuchmacro" was not defined.` |
| ctx.typed-option | `DEF -Z: invalid option \| DEF: options: -p<integer> -c<integer> -b<string> -B<string> -E<string> -t<string>...` | `DEF -Z: invalid option \| DEF: options: -p<integer> -c<integer> -b<string> -B<string> -E<string> -t<string>...` |
